transcript:
This message comes from Schwab.
Investing with Schwab is like a hike with endless trails.
Go solo with self-directed investing,
take stops along the way with trading,
or choose a guide with full service wealth management.
Whatever trails you take, you can invest your way with Schwab.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump is preparing to sit down for a closely-watched meeting.
He's in China for the APEC Summit, the Pacific Rim Leaders.
And his meeting is with both Chinese President Xi Jinping
and Russian leader Vladimir Putin in Piers-Dipa, Shivro.
The focus of his highly-watched meeting with Xi and Putin
is supposed to be about denuclearization.
Though the White House has already said they're not expecting this discussion
to produce any agreement to decrease the number of nuclear weapons.
Even if there are no deliverables from the meeting,
Trump will get the photo op moment
as he tries to cement his legacy on the world stage
in his last two years in office.
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News, Shenzhen.
The artificial intelligence company Anthropic says it put nearly 1 billion shares on the market
in a record-breaking initial public offering of $83 per share.
NPR's Sean Ruich reports.
Just five years old, Anthropic is a powerhouse of the AI world
with the Claude family of models.
Its IPO had been widely anticipated and brings in over $81.3 billion.
That exceeds the $75 billion that Elon Musk's SpaceX raised in its IPO earlier this year.
Anthropic's listing had strong demand
despite coming at a time of growing concern about a possible AI bubble.
Its shares will start trading on the NASDAQ on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT.
And Anthropic is a financial supporter of NPR.
John Ruich, NPR News.
New York Democratic Congressman Hakeem Jeffries is on track to make history
as the nation's first black house speaker.
House Democrats overwhelmingly nominated Jeffries during a closed-door meeting today,
voting 251 to 11, with no votes coming from a group of progressive newcomers.
The full House will vote on Jeffries nomination
when the new Congress convenes in January.
Democrats are questioning whether President Trump's nominee to be Inspector General
of the Interior Department can remain independent.
Dennis Kirk is a Trump loyalist and co-author of the right-wing playbook Project 2025.
And Piers Kirk-Sigler has more.
Democrats say Republicans are ramming this nomination through the lame-duck Congress
before they take over and launch investigations into no-bid contracts given
by the Interior Department for the reflecting pool
and the Secretary's push to sell federal public lands.
Trump's nominee, Dennis Kirk, told Nevada Senator Catherine Cortez-Masto
that if waste, fraud, or abuse allegations surface, he'd review them.
I am concerned about the taxpayer dollars.
Good. So am I. And that even includes this administration.
If they're abusing taxpayer dollars, you'd be willing to look into that.
Thank you.
Then there was a longer pause before the Democratic senator noted that was a non-answer.
The Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee adjourned
without voting to move the nomination forward.
Kirk Sigler, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Results from the midterm elections still coming in.
In Alaska, Republican Nick Begich has won reelection to the state's only House seat.
Begich was endorsed by President Trump in his race as one of the last to be called
by the Associated Press this election cycle.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new agreement
on military cooperation with Venezuela Wednesday.
He made the announcement in Caracas during his first trip to Venezuela
since U.S. Special Forces deposed President Nicolas Maduro last January.
Hegseth said the new agreement ranges from joint training to intelligence sharing.
Researchers are developing brain implants that can help restore people's speech and movement.
And NPR's Ping Huang reports these technologies can even help people sing.
A 58-year-old trained singer had lost much of her ability to speak and sing due to ALS,
a disease that destroys nerve cells that control muscle movement.
Maitreyi Wairakar is a neuroscientist at UC Davis.
She and her colleagues designed an implant that connects to parts
of the singer's brain related to speech, pitch, and tone.
We designed a task to enable her to sing a musical scale.
We asked her to sing a typical major scale, and we were able to decode all the notes
that she sang with very high accuracy.
[Singing]
The implant records her brain signals into a computer, which translates them into commands.
The technology is still largely experimental and was presented
at the Society for Neuroscience conference.
Ping Huang, NPR News.
And I'm Jael Snyder.
This is NPR News.
This message comes from Schwab.
